ROW.COLUMN: (FR/AC) Patterns of Sequentially Numbered Checks, Monetary Instruments

Fraudsters have long recognized that the inherent delays in check processing and clearing produce an opportunity to perpetrate fraud. In addition, improvements in technology make it easier than ever for fraudsters to modify checks, or create counterfeit checks which can be deposited and funds withdrawn before the counterfeit is detected. Electronic check presentment has further confounded this problem because of the shortened window for detection. Check fraud and check kiting schemes typically involve the writing and depositing of checks to and from the same (external and internal) accounts. Sometimes these schemes can be detected through the sequential numbering present on checks written on, or deposited into, the account or accounts involved in the kiting or fraud scheme. This scenario monitors for accounts for which large or unusual numbers of checks or monetary instruments are being deposited into, or written on, the account.

There are two main datasets in this scenario. The first selects accounts which have MI-transactions for the look back period and at least one transaction for the frequency period. This dataset is the start of the sequence. The second dataset selects all MI-transactions for the look-back period. One more dataset is used for the properly end of the pattern. The sort order of the datasets in the pattern includes the focal entity, the product code, name, routing number and serial number of the monetary instruments of the transactions.
All monetary instruments are divided on three types: true-sequenced events (when conditions for a single episode are met); false-sequenced events (when conditions for a single episode are not met), non-sequenced events.
For the true-sequenced events aggregate values are counted. In the end of the sequence (a record for another Focal Entity or End-of-Stream event) conditions for episodes are checked, and if necessary the match is raised.

select case when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 1 then add_months(add_days(kc.CLNDR_DT, 1), 120) -- 10 years after the current date when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 0 then add_months(kc.CLNDR_DT, -120) end DDATE, -- 10 years before the current date case when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 1 then '246060999' -- slightly higher than highest possible time string when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 0 then '000000000' end DTIME, -- This field was set to type 'Time' in dataset editor, but treated like a string case when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 1 then '~' -- printable character with highest ASCII value when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 0 then '!' end DSTRING, -- printable character with lowest ASCII value case when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 1 then 999999999 -- 9 digits maximum for INT when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 0 then 0 end DINT, case when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 1 then 9999999999999999 -- 16 digits maximum for FLOAT when kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE = 0 then 0.0 end DFLOAT, kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE from @MANTAS@.KDD_cal kc where kc.CLNDR_DAY_AGE in (0,1) AND kc.CLNDR_NM = 'SYSCAL'
